The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt. An action role-playing game developed by CD Projekt Red, released in 2015 for PC, PlayStation 4, and Xbox One. You assume the role of Geralt of Rivia, a witcher or monster hunter, pursuing the villainous Wild Hunt across a richly detailed fantasy world while searching for his lost love. Its branching narrative, morally complex characters, and expansive quests elevated storytelling in open-world games. The narrative branches heavily on your choices—dialogue options alter quest outcomes and NPC fates, and even minor decisions ripple across the story in unexpected ways. Three expansions, Hearts of Stone and Blood and Wine, add thirty hours of content and are praised as equal to the base game in quality, with many considering them superior. Monster hunting drives exploration as you research creatures, gather specific oils and potions, and exploit weaknesses, and combat requires preparation and learning enemy patterns. Alchemy and crafting systems reward potion management as you balance carrying weight and strategically prepare for tough encounters. Side quests are narrative-rich, with even minor tasks having compelling backstories, moral dilemmas, and character development often absent from routine quests in other games. The Bloody Baron quest became a talking point for its emotionally mature storytelling, subverting typical fantasy tropes and exploring domestic abuse and loss. The game was published in Poland by CD Projekt Red, not a mainstream Western studio at the time, proving that independent studios could rival AAA narrative ambition.
